# HisabIQ Free-First Business Model — Owner Decision Record

**Decision date:** 25 October 2026 (Asia/Dhaka)  
**Status:** Owner-approved commercial direction and gated pilot specification. Not a public price announcement or authorization to implement, merge, spend funds, contact merchants or change production.  
**Approval context:** After receiving the Bangladesh business-model report and recommendation, the owner replied: “Okay write this dicision”. This records acceptance of that direction while preserving its explicit research and launch conditions.

## Authority and related documents

> **Latest owner decision:** [Section 10](#10-final-amendment--three-levels-of-interface-capability-across-every-module) defines the final ERP-wide UI ladder: Basic = simple; Medium = interconnectivity with limited richness; Premium = full information and functionality. It takes precedence over earlier interface-packaging statements.

This decision supersedes conflicting commercial proposals in the earlier free-first strategy and Control Center reference design. The original research remains available as historical rationale.

- [Full Bangladesh market research, economics and decision report](2026-10-25-hisabiq-bangladesh-business-model-report.md)
- [Earlier free-first proposal](2026-10-25-hisabiq-free-first-hybrid-monetization-strategy.md)
- [Control Center reference design](2026-10-25-hisabiq-saas-control-center-nestshererp-reference-design.md)
- [Original market-review brief](2026-10-25-astra-bangladesh-pricing-and-free-first-review-brief.md)

The full report's recommendations, detailed limits, refund terms and Keep / Change / Reject / Test table are adopted as the pilot baseline, subject to the validation conditions below. Prices chosen for testing are not proven willingness-to-pay. Scenario conversion rates, costs and revenue remain assumptions.

## 1. Commercial principle

HisabIQ must be useful indefinitely before payment. Acquire the first 1,000 distinct verified business registrations, measure activation and retained use, and earn purchases through clear business value.

A Free business buying SMS or optional features is a valuable paying customer. Subscription conversion is not mandatory. Registrations, activated businesses, D30 retention, MAU, unique payers and subscribers must be reported separately.

The first 1,000 registrations are a funded validation milestone, not a profitability promise.

## 2. Subscription catalog

Four tiers only: Free, Counter, Pro and Plus. Medium becomes Pro; Premium becomes Plus in the future approved catalog migration. Existing customer contracts must be honored.

| Item | Free | Counter | Pro | Plus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly price | ৳0 | ৳199 | ৳399 | ৳599 |
| Named users, including owner | 1 | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| Active products | 500 | 2,000 | 10,000 | 20,000 |
| Attachment capacity | 25 MB | 100 MB | 500 MB | 2 GB |
| Basic ERP, reports, receipt printing and export | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| Saved quotations/templates, batch print and barcode convenience | — | Included | Included | Included |
| Advanced reports | Optional pass | Optional pass | Included | Included |
| Optional integrated advanced workflows | — | — | When ready | When ready |

All tiers are one business/one shop in V1. There is no multi-branch, offline or unlimited messaging promise. No mandatory setup fee.

Prices are intended total customer prices. Obtain SKU-specific tax confirmation before publication; the report's 15% reserve is a financial assumption, not a tax ruling.

Annual subscriptions are deferred until service stability and two paid months of experience. Pilot baseline: 12 months for 11 monthly payments—Counter ৳2,189, Pro ৳4,389, Plus ৳6,589. Manual monthly renewal remains default.

## 3. Permanent Free offering and trust boundaries

Free includes ordinary sales, purchases, returns, expenses, stock and party ledgers; cash/bank/MFS recording; compound units; split payments; basic owner profit, sales, due, expense and low-stock summaries; ordinary A4/thermal receipts, PDFs, statements, reprints and data export.

Do not charge per ordinary sale or print. Do not put security, tenant isolation, audit integrity, backups or financial correctness behind an add-on.

No commercial monthly transaction/customer cap in the pilot. Publish technical abuse safeguards and monitor real costs.

On downgrade, preserve records and existing products. Allow routine transactions with existing products even above the lower catalog cap; restrict new catalog expansion rather than making the shop read-only. Preserve historical settlement, correction, return, reprint and export rights. Existing attachments remain readable/downloadable; new uploads follow quota. Independently purchased passes and owned print packs survive unrelated subscription changes.

Start users on Free immediately. Reject an automatic full-suite 15/30-day countdown. Offer a contextual, optional seven-day advanced-report trial after useful data exists.

## 4. Optional purchases

| Purchase | Pilot baseline |
|---|---|
| Reports Plus | ৳99 for seven days or ৳199 for 30 days |
| Extra attachment capacity | ৳99 for 30 days; +1 GB total capacity, not another accumulating GB every renewal |
| Optional invoice-design pack | ৳149 once per business, retained while HisabIQ operates; no lifetime hosting promise |
| Guided configuration | ৳399, up to 30 scheduled minutes |
| Guided setup/import | ৳999, up to 60 minutes; one clean CSV, up to 500 products and 200 parties |
| Complex migration | Diagnostic from ৳1,999/up to two hours; implementation separately quoted |

Reject a universal ৳149 monthly feature price. Test Reports 30-day access at ৳149 versus ৳199; ৳199 is the central baseline. Defer ৳49 purchases until automated payment and support costs are measured.

Launch SMS after reconciliation works, then an evidence-backed report pass. Storage follows secure uploads; print designs follow demonstrated demand. Avoid a crowded store or general-purpose credit currency.

Owner-only purchasing initially. Show price, term, expiry, inclusions and a clear decline choice. Manual renewal by default. Credit unused actual paid value of overlapping passes/subscription time on upgrade. Never double-charge for an included benefit.

Adopt the report's first-purchase refund, duplicate/failed fulfillment and unused annual-term policies. Consumed SMS remains subject to the explicit delivery/billing policy.

## 5. SMS

| Non-masking pack | Price |
|---|---:|
| 100 billable segments | ৳99 |
| 500 billable segments | ৳399 |
| 2,000 billable segments | ৳1,499 |

These replace the earlier ৳89/৳349/৳1,299 hypotheses. Publication requires effective landed supplier cost at most ৳0.40/segment and measured contribution of at least 30% of tax-exclusive revenue.

Obtain three written quotes and test two providers. Verify current contracting authority, reseller rights, taxes, MNP, validity, sender requirements, failure charging and delivery reconciliation. Do not treat advertised tariffs or delivery claims as contracted performance.

Credits have 12-month validity, visible expiry, reminders and carry-forward on recharge under published terms. Do not rely on expired credits for profit. No unlimited SMS/WhatsApp or monthly SMS allowance by tier; permit a controlled five-segment activation sample.

Bill provider segments, including Bangla/Unicode concatenation; show estimated recipient × segment cost before sending. Reserve, dispatch and reconcile credits with idempotency; no blind duplicate retries or credits from frontend success alone.

Keep credit liability distinct from earned revenue and wholesale costs. Authentication OTP is a platform cost. Masking is quote-only initially; it is not promised to every shop.

## 6. Support and Control Center

Free includes essential instructions, issue reporting, account-access assistance and product-fault resolution. Severity drives security/data-integrity response across all plans.

Initial support hours: Saturday–Thursday, 10:00–18:00 Bangladesh time, with published holidays and founder/rota coverage.

| Tier | Routine first-response target | Included scheduled help |
|---|---|---|
| Free | Two business days | Group orientation and one optional 10-minute activation callback |
| Counter | One business day | One 15-minute setup session once |
| Pro | One business day, priority queue | Setup plus one 15-minute configuration session/quarter |
| Plus | Four support hours | Setup plus one 15-minute configuration session/month |

These are pilot operational targets, not contractual resolution guarantees. No dedicated engineer or unlimited configuration at ৳599. Product bug fixes do not consume paid assistance allowances.

Reuse the existing SaaS shell, tickets, Sales column picker and React components. ByabsIQ remains the backend. Adapt NestSherERP's typed settings/dependency/audit patterns; never reuse its permissive entitlement stub as production gating.

Keep commercial entitlement, presentation settings, employee authorization and support delegation separate. Hiding Profit is a preference; denying employee access to profit requires server-side filtering across APIs, reports, details, exports and print.

Initial remote configuration uses exact, customer-approved setting commands: target business/user, key, value, before/after, revision, ticket and actual support actor. Consent is single-use and valid for 15 minutes; retries are idempotent. Customer sees history and Undo.

No unrestricted impersonation, copied sessions or requested passwords/OTPs/PINs. Staff identity, MFA, scoped access, revocation and audit are required. Live read-only support visits are deferred until repeated need justifies them.

Bound complimentary reports trials to seven days, once per business per 90 days, within an approved budget and audit. Refund/payment/ownership powers stay separate.

## 7. Financial and acquisition direction

The report's monthly scenarios for 1,000 registrations are planning cases:

| Metric | Pessimistic | Expected | Optimistic |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MAU | 180 | 350 | 650 |
| Gross billings | ৳9,944 | ৳56,076 | ৳165,478 |
| Operating result before founder/engineering and income tax | −৳35,567 | −৳13,272 | ৳18,282 |
| Result including assumed ৳80,000 founder/engineering | −৳115,567 | −৳93,272 | −৳61,718 |

Do not present these figures as forecasts or earned cash from unconsumed SMS balances.

Use approximately ৳6.3 lakh as the fully costed 90-day planning envelope after launch readiness, including contingency; approximately ৳3.4 lakh cash if founder/engineering compensation is deferred. These are budget estimates, not authorization to spend or proof that pre-launch development is funded.

Focus initial cohorts on hardware/electrical in reachable local markets; then selective fabric/furniture. Defer pharmacy/high-throughput grocery until relevant correctness, speed and connectivity constraints are proven.

Use market demonstrations, verified referrals, small partner channels and Bangla tutorials. Reward retained verified referrals rather than empty signups. The report's initial acquisition budget is ৳100,000 cash for 1,000 registrations, subject to channel tests.

## 8. Gates and order of work

1. Verify the actual sale/purchase/return → stock → payment → party-ledger workflow, tenant isolation, error recovery and backup restoration.
2. Reconcile ByabsIQ's older PRO/PREMIUM trial/read-only policy with the permanent Free decision.
3. Approve implementation contracts separately for catalog, orders, settlement, grants, SMS ledger, expiry and refunds.
4. Integrate narrow consented support configuration and real supplier/payment services.
5. Validate actual report data and secure attachments before charging for them.
6. Begin the 90-day merchant experiment only after readiness.

Pilot gates: activation at least 50%; D30 retention at least 50% of activated mature cohorts; capacity below 75% planned support load; SMS margin at least 30%; credible retained-customer payback within six months; no unresolved critical money, stock, access or restore failures. These are management thresholds, not research findings.

Continue late-cohort D30 measurement through day 120. Pause acquisition on wrong-tenant access, unexplained ledger discrepancies, duplicate fulfillment or failed restoration. Validate demand and direct contribution before scaling beyond the first cohort.

## 9. Remaining validation and exclusions

Owner acceptance settles the commercial direction. It does not establish merchant willingness to pay, tax status, supplier reliability, hired support cost, production readiness or actual conversion/churn. Those require the report's interviews, paid experiments, contracts and operational checks.

The report's full Keep / Change / Reject / Test table remains the detailed decision matrix. Its Test and Later items remain experiments or deferrals, not approved immediate features.

No code implementation, automatic merging, public price announcement, customer outreach, provider purchase, deployment or production change is authorized by this documentation task. Next work requires a separately scoped instruction.

## 10. Final amendment — three levels of interface capability across every module

**Date:** 25 October 2026 (Asia/Dhaka).  
**Status:** Final owner choice.  
**Owner clarification:** “Basic see simple UI without details information and interconnectivity. Medium get interconnectivity but not get fully information richness and premium full functionality”.

This amendment supersedes any earlier statement treating Medium and Premium as the same full interface. It also supersedes conflicting interface-packaging recommendations in the research report. The final model is **Basic = simple**, **Medium = connected**, **Premium = connected and information-rich**.

Names in this amendment follow the owner's terminology: Basic is Free; Medium corresponds to the previously recorded Pro tier; Premium corresponds to Plus. This clarification does not change prices or authorize a deployed plan-code rename. Counter retains its previously specified package benefits; this message does not assign it the whole Medium or Premium interface.

### 10.1 ERP-wide behavior

| Capability | Basic / Free | Medium / Pro | Premium / Plus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default screen | Simple workable interface | Connected interface with restrained detail | Full information-rich interface |
| Table information | Essential fields only | Essential fields plus selected operational fields | All implemented optional fields and rich details, subject to employee permission |
| Cross-module record links | Plain names/references; use normal module navigation | Enabled | Enabled |
| Customer name in Sales History | Plain text | Opens customer ledger | Opens customer ledger |
| Invoice reference in Party Ledger | Reference text | Opens invoice | Opens invoice |
| Receive payment from a selected invoice | Use the standard payment workflow | Contextual payment action available | Contextual payment action available |
| Party Ledger item/payment breakdowns and extra visual detail | Omitted from the simple table | Limited detail; no full rich table | Full implemented details, breakdowns, indicators and expansion controls |
| Sales/Product optional columns | Fixed essential baseline plus common preferences | A restricted operational set | Full eligible column catalog and defaults |
| Advanced Settings | Common settings | Workflow connections and permitted operational settings | Full eligible display/detail/column/workflow controls |
| Ability to simplify the interface further | Common preferences | May turn available connections/details off | May turn available connections/details off |

Basic users retain a complete standard route to essential work: for example, open Sales to find an invoice, Parties to find a customer, or the standard payment workflow to record money. The Basic list itself does not provide the paid cross-module shortcuts. Do not leave dead clickable names, fake buttons or unexplained disabled actions in simple tables.

Medium adds interconnectivity and contextual actions but does not automatically unlock every optional column, expanded item breakdown, indicator, summary or advanced information panel. Premium receives the full implemented rich experience and its configuration controls.

“Full functionality” refers to the implemented ERP UI and workflows within the purchased commercial scope. It does not mean unlimited SMS, unlimited storage/support, bypassing employee permissions, unfinished integrations or features explicitly deferred in V1. Other previously recorded quotas and historical-data protections remain applicable.

### 10.2 Apply to all modules

Review Dashboard, POS/Counter, Sales and Returns, Purchases and Returns, Products/Inventory, Parties/Ledger, Finance/Expenses/Daybook, Reports, and any enabled vendor, bundle, installment, quotation or online-sales workspace.

For each module, list:
1. Essential fields/actions that make the Basic workflow usable.
2. Cross-module links and contextual actions provided by Medium and Premium.
3. Rich optional information provided by Premium.
4. Settings controlling each available capability and its tenant/user scope.
5. The standard Basic route to complete each essential action.

This is a module-by-module application of the same policy, not a request for unrelated redesigns or new modules. Existing components and current design rules remain the implementation authority.

### 10.3 Settings and effective behavior

The Settings module must expose precise ERP-wide controls, grouped by module: default table columns, optional detail sections, transaction indicators, expandable rows, record links and contextual actions.

A plan decides which controls and capabilities are available. The customer decides which of those available capabilities to enable. A customer preference cannot enable a capability outside their plan or an independently purchased grant.

Use distinct stable capabilities for interconnectivity and information richness; do not implement one `advancedUI` boolean that gives Medium all Premium details. Existing standalone add-on grants remain valid only for the specific capability purchased; purchasing a report pass does not silently upgrade the whole ERP interface.

Customer-owned settings, employee permissions, commercial entitlements and support delegation remain separate. Support can configure only eligible settings with the previously approved consent/audit safeguards. Premium owners can choose a simple interface; staff still see only what their permissions allow.

Financial amounts, balances, source references, required warnings and historical records must remain correct and accessible through the authorized standard workflow. Simplified tables do not change accounting rules or delete underlying data.

### 10.4 Implementation boundary

This records the final packaging choice. The next implementation specification must inventory every module against this three-level matrix, reconcile existing plan/grant behavior and reuse the current settings/UI components. No application code, public prices, backend enforcement or production configuration is changed by recording this amendment.

## 11. Approved Recycle Bin and recovery policy

**Decision date:** 25 October 2026 (Asia/Dhaka).  
**Status:** Owner-approved product direction, recorded after the owner accepted the Recycle Bin recommendation with “Okay done”. Implementation is a separate task.

### 11.1 Purpose and plan availability

Provide **Settings → Recycle Bin** for recovering accidental deletions. Basic recovery is available on every plan, including Free; it is a data-protection capability and is not removed by the simplified Basic interface policy.

Ordinary eligible deleted records have a **30-day recovery window**. Show their expiry clearly. Offer a short **Undo** action immediately after a successful deletion. Undo follows the same permissions, validation and audit rules as Restore.

Longer recovery for eligible nonfinancial records and advanced recovery filters are possible Premium enhancements; no extended duration or additional price is finalized here.

### 11.2 Record-specific behavior

| Record | Approved behavior |
|---|---|
| Draft sales, quotations, templates and notes | Move eligible records to the Bin; restore with validation |
| Products or parties with no transaction history | Move to the Bin only after dependency checks; restore after duplicate/conflict checks |
| Products or parties linked to transactions | Archive instead of deleting their historical identity; reactivate through the archive workflow |
| Posted sales invoices, purchases, expenses and payments | Use authorized, source-linked cancellation or accounting reversal; do not treat them as ordinary restorable Bin records |
| Individual ledger projections/entries | Correct through their originating transaction; no independent delete/restore |

A posted cancellation or reversal preserves its original document, accounting/stock effects and audit trail. Reinstatement, where supported, must be a validated correction/reposting workflow with current dependency, payment, stock and period checks. It must never silently reactivate an old transaction and duplicate its effects.

The 30-day window does not authorize destruction of posted financial history or audit records. Financial retention follows the separate applicable retention policy.

### 11.3 Minimum UI

Display record/module, recognizable name or reference, deletion time, deleting user, recovery deadline and eligible Restore action. Provide search and basic module filters on every plan. Explain why a record cannot be restored and link or direct the authorized user to the appropriate correction/archive workflow.

Do not expose another employee's restricted records simply because they are in the Bin. A list or preview remains subject to tenant isolation and record/field permissions.

There is no ordinary **Empty Bin** action for posted financial records. Permanent deletion and retention expiry for other records require a separately defined safe policy; this decision does not authorize bulk destructive cleanup.

### 11.4 Restore integrity and authority

The tenant owner controls delete/restore permissions; having a paid plan does not grant every employee permission. Server-side checks must validate current tenant membership, authority, dependencies, record state and identifier conflicts.

Examples: a recreated product code, duplicate party identifier, archived parent or already-restored record must produce a clear safe result. Never overwrite a replacement record, merge parties automatically, cascade-restore unrelated records or silently recreate missing dependencies.

Record the actual actor, business, original deletion, restoration, timestamps and outcome in the audit trail. Restore must preserve record identity and relationships, be atomic where related changes are required, and be idempotent under repeated clicks/retries. Restoring a draft must not post a sale, change stock or move money.

Support engineers do not gain general delete/restore powers through configuration access; any assistance must use separately authorized, consented scopes.

### 11.5 Acceptance for eventual implementation

- An authorized user deletes an eligible draft and can Undo or restore it within 30 days.
- Basic users retain the same essential recovery rights.
- Unauthorized users and foreign tenants cannot list, preview, delete or restore the record.
- Duplicate identifiers, changed dependencies, expired recovery windows and concurrent restore requests are handled without overwrites or duplicate effects.
- Archive/reactivation preserves transaction-linked products and parties.
- Posted transactions and ledger entries cannot bypass audited correction/reversal rules through the Bin.
- Delete and Restore are traceable, and routine data recovery does not require purchasing an upgrade.

No code, merge, deployment, public pricing or production data change is authorized by recording this decision.

## 12. Tenant diagnostic logs — SaaS-only support access

**Decision date:** 25 October 2026 (Asia/Dhaka).  
**Status:** Owner-requested product requirement. Implementation remains a separate task.

### 12.1 Placement and purpose

Every tenant must have separately scoped technical diagnostic logs so authorized support engineers can investigate reported problems. Expose them through **SaaS Dashboard → Tenants → Selected business → Diagnostics / Logs** and ticket-linked diagnostics. Do not add a technical-log viewer or raw technical-log download to the customer's normal ERP interface.

This requirement applies to all plans. Diagnosing a HisabIQ fault does not require a customer upgrade.

“SaaS-only” describes visibility in the product UI; it does not authorize undisclosed collection of arbitrary business data. The customer-facing privacy/support information must describe diagnostic collection and authorized staff access.

### 12.2 Separate diagnostic events from business records

Technical diagnostics include error codes, failed requests, validation categories, duration, retry outcomes, release/build version, affected module/action, server timestamp, request/correlation ID and an internal authorized tenant/user reference where needed.

Business transaction history, original invoices, balances, source-linked corrections and owner-visible support/configuration changes remain in their existing authorized workflows. This decision does not remove customer access to their own records or replace the business audit trail with hidden technical logs.

Platform security/access audit is also a separate protected record, including who viewed or exported diagnostics. A diagnostic viewer must not grant permission to alter business transactions, financial evidence or audit history.

### 12.3 Tenant attribution and privacy

Backend log attribution uses the authenticated session and validated membership/business context. Never trust a browser-supplied tenant ID as proof of context. Frontend errors are untrusted telemetry: validate/redact/rate-limit them and attach authoritative tenant context server-side. Preserve the business context at the time of the event when users switch businesses.

Use structured, allowlisted event fields and safe error categories. Exclude passwords, OTPs, PINs, session cookies/tokens, authorization headers, payment credentials, raw payment proof, attachment contents and unnecessary names/phone numbers or financial values.

Do not collect full request/response bodies, entire localStorage, typed form values, screen recordings or database dumps by default. Stack traces and third-party error messages require sanitization before storage/display because they can include sensitive values.

Authentication failures before tenant context is established belong in separate restricted platform diagnostics; do not assign them to a guessed tenant.

### 12.4 Support workflow and authorization

1. Open the relevant support ticket and select the verified business.
2. View recent safe diagnostic events for that business, filtered by date, module, severity, action, error code or correlation ID.
3. Link the relevant event/correlation to the ticket and record the diagnosis.
4. If more evidence is necessary, use a separately authorized, bounded diagnostic action or the existing consented support process.

Standard access to minimal redacted technical metadata follows a dedicated platform diagnostics permission and assigned tenant/ticket scope; it does not require unrestricted customer impersonation. Access to business records, attachments or sensitive data requires its own authority and applicable customer consent. A ticket or log-view permission does not itself grant that authority.

Enforce tenant and staff scope on the server for list, detail, search and export. A filtered frontend over unrestricted logs is insufficient. Search must not reveal other tenants through suggestions, counts, error messages or correlation lookups.

Show staff identity and access purpose in the protected access audit. Record log viewing/export and sensitive diagnostic actions, require additional export permission, and keep exports redacted and limited. Support cannot edit/delete evidence or grant themselves broader access.

### 12.5 Reliability and minimum UI

The SaaS view should show readable error summaries, event time, module/action, severity, result, release and correlation ID, with safe details on expansion. Distinguish frontend-reported events from authoritative backend outcomes; an error event alone does not prove that a sale/payment failed to commit.

Link retry/commit outcomes by correlation or operation ID so support can distinguish a lost response from an unposted transaction. Logging must not duplicate business operations or expose an action to replay financial requests directly.

Collection, storage and search need bounded event sizes, rate limits, appropriate sampling and a documented retention policy before deployment. Do not promise unlimited logs or indefinite diagnostic retention. Keep required transaction/security audit evidence under its own policy, outside sampled diagnostic streams.

### 12.6 Acceptance for eventual implementation

- Authorized support can diagnose a ticket using only the selected tenant's safe events.
- Customers cannot open the internal diagnostic viewer or retrieve raw logs through an ERP API.
- Staff without the correct scope cannot access another tenant through IDs, searches, exports or correlated-event links.
- Secret-bearing requests and representative failure cases produce redacted events.
- Business switching attributes each event to its actual authorized context.
- Diagnostic access is audited; ordinary support cannot erase logs or use them to mutate stock, money or permissions.
- Customer business history and consented-change history remain available through their authorized workflows.

This records the product requirement; no application code, deployment or production logging configuration is changed.

## 15. ERP-wide KISS refinement

The owner requested that KISS be applied to UI/UX after the complete Settings, SaaS and commerce requirements were assembled.

The [ERP-wide KISS contract](2026-10-25-hisabiq-erp-wide-kiss-uiux-contract.md) now governs screen composition and progressive disclosure: common actions first, one clear primary action, fewer screens/tabs, relevant defaults, reused components and shorter copy. It takes precedence over earlier optional layout/step suggestions while preserving approved plan differences and safety requirements.

The five-tab tenant workspace, one module selector, conditional impact review and shared checkout are planning choices implementing this instruction. They do not change prices, grants, data retention, verification, support consent or backend authority. Premium is fully capable without expanding every detail by default; Basic remains workable and Medium connected.

This is a documentation/design-plan refinement. Application UI implementation, backend integration, merge and deployment have not started.
